\label{sec:gen-acceptance-tests}

\begin{sloppypar}
The titles are the blueprint's (\code{protocol-blueprint.md:1261-1359} at \code{b435631}); the
numbers are the blueprint's too, and are how its text and this report cite the tests. Test
files are under \file{tests/LeanerVMTests/}. \enquote{Not
built} means that the layer defining the witness is not on \code{main} at \code{b435631}, so the
test cannot yet reject anything. The verdict says whether the test states what leanVM does and
whether its witness rejects what the test says, with the register rows that bear on it
(\cref{sec:reg}) or, where no row does, the dossier and section that examined the test.
\end{sloppypar}

1 & Fingerprint degree
  & \lean{sideProduct_collision} carries the factor 4 (Layer 5)
  & not built
  & right: the error is $4·2^μ/\abs{\E}$, as the specification says (\file{gt-bus.md} §C) \\
2 & Padding leaves are 1
  & the honest run of Layer 6 on a one-row witness
  & not built
  & right: states what the pinned sources do (\file{gt-bus.md} §C) \\
3 & \code{R_c ≠ 0} is load-bearing
  & the Layer 6 mutation with a zero count, rejected by \lean{busPhase}
  & not built
  & right (\file{gt-bus.md} §C) \\
4 & One root, not two
  & \lean{verify_iff_compiled} pins the stream's shape
  & not built
  & right (\file{gt-bus.md} §C); the status finding it cites is an agreement of the three
  sources, not a divergence (\code{R95}) \\
5 & Domain separators
  & two tuples distinguished by \lean{leanIsaTables} flush polynomials
  & no: \lean{leanIsaTables} exists nowhere (the ensemble is \lean{leanIsaEnsemble})
  & a test of the arithmetization, not of the proof system (\file{gt-bus.md} §C); names a
  declaration that does not exist (\code{R92}) \\
6 & Zerocheck point recycling
  & none; \enquote{the state function of Layer 7 charges the zerocheck to Layer 6's challenges}
  & not built
  & right that the point must follow the commitment; the charge cannot be meant literally, a
  phase's state function charging that phase's own challenges, and it is over-charged elsewhere
  (\code{R47}) \\
7 & Back-loaded padding
  & \lean{sumCube_prodVars}; \lean{tableSummand_target} on heights 2 and 1
  & the lemma named is another (the one meant, \lean{sumCube_padHigh}, is on \code{main});
  \lean{tableSummand_target} is not built; a test that does the job exists
  (\file{tests/…/Protocol/Padding.lean:44-49})
  & names the wrong lemma and a witness that does not exist (\code{R82}) \\
8 & Degree three, three scalars
  & \lean{RoundPoly.decode} on the dumped proof
  & not built
  & right: three coefficients on the wire, $c_1$ derived (\file{gt-opening-compile.md} §C.3);
  the oracle protocol's four coefficients and round check are a deviation that owes a transport
  lemma (\code{R53}) \\
9 & Shared bus powers
  & \lean{tableSummand_target} fails with per-table powers on two tables
  & not built
  & right for leanISA; stated on Layer 7's \lean{rem}, which the spine does not have, and no
  convention fixes which claim of \lean{BusOut} takes which power (\file{gt-table-pub.md} §E.4;
  \code{R2}) \\
10 & Top limb of the public input
  & the Layer 8 mutation with a nonzero \code{mem_2} at cell 0 and the third claim dropped
  & yes, as \texttt{\#guard}s on the pool of a toy-shaped instance
  (\file{tests/…/Protocol/PublicInput.lean:151-180}), not as a mutation of the phase
  & a test on the pool, not a theorem: every theorem of the phase holds for an instance with two
  lines; the witness to name is the adaptor's, when built (\code{R54}) \\
11 & Joint list binding
  & the joint invariant of \lean{whirOpen_rbrSoundness}; \lean{verify_knowledgeSound} extracts
  the member
  & not built
  & the right words; the list-binding compilation it rests on is a theorem the blueprint names
  and does not state (\code{R24}) \\
12 & Absorb before squeeze
  & \lean{FsState} follows the stream order; \lean{verify_iff_compiled}
  & not built
  & right: sizes and root are absorbed before the first challenge (\file{gt-bus.md} §C) \\
13 & Index column bit order
  & the \texttt{\#guard}s on \lean{idxColumn 2}
  & yes (\file{tests/…/Protocol/FixedColumns.lean:37-47}); they fail on the reversed
  order
  & met (\file{code-layer1.md} §F.2) \\
14 & Bytecode slot bits
  & \lean{bytecodeColumn_slot} on a two-instruction program
  & yes, but it restates the definition and holds of the swapped layout by the same proof
  & names a tautology; the witness that pins the slot is \lean{bytecodeColumn_answer_boolVec},
  and no test compares the column with leanVM's encoder (\code{R79}) \\
15 & Selector alignment
  & three blocks of sizes 4, 2, 1 with the small one first
  & yes (\file{tests/…/Protocol/Stack.lean:87-95})
  & overclaims: largest first is sufficient, not necessary (sizes 1, 1, 2 are aligned), and 4, 2,
  1 are heights, not sizes (\code{R80}) \\
16 & Variable order
  & the honest run of Layer 7 with two heights
  & not built
  & right (\file{gt-table-pub.md} §4, item 5) \\
17 & Radix and parity
  & \lean{verify_iff_compiled} on the dumped proof
  & not built
  & right; it should also count the combiner drawn after the last layer (\code{R9}) \\
18 & Counts in the count tree
  & the dumped proof
  & not built
  & right; its clause \enquote{the leaf layout, and so $ζ$, differ} is loose: a different count
  stack changes the count side's selectors, not $ζ$'s length (\file{gt-bus.md} §C) \\
19 & The extractor reads the stack
  & \lean{witnessOf_stackOf}
  & not built (Layer 3)
  & its witness is not a Lean statement as written; three equalities under
  \lean{SatisfiedBy} are (\code{R69}) \\
20 & Perfect completeness needs no exceptional-challenge clause
  & \lean{piop_perfectCompleteness} has no side condition on challenges
  & yes: the theorem is proved, with none
  & to be rewritten: the inverse at $r_{\mathrm{eq}} = 1$ is the pinned Rust prover's, a
  completeness defect of an implementation, not part of \lean{flockError} (\code{R17}; the
  disagreement \code{R4}; the Rust prover \code{R111}) \\
21 & Sizes are parameters
  & \lean{verify_iff_compiled} quantifies $∃\, s$
  & not built
  & a deliberate deviation, rightly kept; it records the dispatch and not the bound, uniform over
  the announced sizes, that it owes (\code{R6}) \\
22 & Tags, not labels
  & the dumped proof
  & not built
  & not examined as a test; the four tags it states are the chain's
  (\file{gt-opening-compile.md} §C.1) \\
23 & Numeric error
  & \lean{piopError_le} at the caps
  & not built
  & leaves out ring switching's $2^{-160}$, which dominates Flock's $2^{-183}$ (\code{R58}); true
  only with the stacking window in \lean{Sizes.Admissible} (\code{R33}); measures the oracle
  protocol's interactive error, not the deployed security level (\code{R23}) \\
24 & The extractor computes
  & the spine's \code{rfl} test on \lean{piopExtractor}; \texttt{\#guard witnessOf (stackOf w) = w}
  & in part: the \code{rfl} test exists and covers zero-round phases only; the
  \texttt{\#guard} cannot be written (no decidable equality on the witness)
  & the extracted stack is not a definition, and with the public-input phase in the bundle the
  test is ill-typed (\code{R46}); computable is not efficient (\code{R48}); the existential forms
  carry no knowledge content (\code{R1}) \\
25 & The wall holds
  & \code{grep -rn 'import LeanerVM.Arithmetization' LeanerVM/Protocol}
  & yes; it lists one exception the convention does not name (\file{LeanerVM/Protocol/Basic.lean})
  & its witness text is false, and the rule has no script (\code{R44}) \\
26 & Seams are the contract
  & \lean{Phases.Complete.toDef}, \lean{Phases.Security.toDef}; the test's \lean{trivComplete}
  & yes
  & met by construction; says nothing about content, a bundle of five phases that check nothing
  typechecking as well (\file{code-spine.md} §E.3; \code{R5}) \\
27 & The toy instance is honest
  & the \texttt{\#guard}s of \file{tests/…/Protocol/Spine.lean}
  & yes
  & met; the fifth clause, the auxiliary predicate, is untestable on the toy
  (\file{code-spine.md} §E.3) \\
28 & The bus seam bounds the degree
  & \lean{Seam.bus} carries \code{totalDegree ≤ I.d}; the tests reject the cubic term
  & yes
  & met as a conjunct; its cost is a guard in the table phase (\code{R2}), and a second side
